entries.title: Alpenzeitung, 26 September 1933, page 3
text: “Zwei Jahre Drusus-Brücke.” An anniversary column: the measurements again, and the justification of the name. “Die Brücke trägt den Namen des römischen Feldherrn Drusus, der 15 Jahre vor Christi Geburt mit seinen Legionen unsere Alpengebiete eroberte.”
The halftone beside it shows the bridge with an eagle column in the foreground: a press picture of the eagles in place. Four captures taken by hand from the library's viewer.
facts: Page 3 'Aus Bolzano Stadt und Land'; four hand captures from the Teßmann digital viewer, 22 October 2026 (manifest)

The article 'Zwei Jahre Drusus-Brücke' repeats the figures (102.3 m, middle span 34.7 m, side spans 21.65 m, roadway 14 m, sidewalks 2 m) and calls the bridge one of the monumental works of recent years, needed for the new Bolzano-Castelfirmiano road and the shorter Merano road via S. Maurizio (notes 07, §2, [V])

Romanità passage: 'Die Brücke trägt den Namen des römischen Feldherrn Drusus, der 15 Jahre vor Christi Geburt mit seinen Legionen unsere Alpengebiete eroberte, Straßen zog, Siedlungen gründete, römische Kultur in die von Sümpfen und Wildbächen durchtobten Täler trug.' (notes 07, §2, [T])
The halftone shows the bridge with the eagle columns in place: a usable 1933 press image of the eagles (notes 07, §2)
Seen in the image: the page head 'Aus Bolzano Stadt und Land' is set in a heavy slanted roman script, the headline 'Zwei Jahre Drusus-Brücke' and the text in Fraktur

Seen in the image: the halftone shows an arched stone bridge with a tall pier column topped by a bird figure in the foreground, lamp posts and a hillside behind; the whole-page capture shows the page on the black ground of the viewer, with zoom and rotate buttons at top right
Rights: the captures are study copies of the viewer; the page is out of copyright, and Teßmann serves it with a 'Downloaden / Drucken' button for proper downloads (manifest)
